title: Career Roadmap: Data Analyst
summary: A Data Analyst transforms raw data into meaningful insights that help organisations understand performance, identify problems, measure results, and make informed decisions. This career combines statistics, SQL, spreadsheets, data visualisation, business understanding, and communication.

blocks.text: For students pursuing a B.Sc. in Data Science & Artificial Intelligence, Data Analyst is a strong entry-level career target because the degree can build both analytical foundations and practical programming skills.

rows.text: 3 years; some institutions offer a 4-year honours or research pathway
Statistics, mathematics, programming, databases, machine learning, and data visualisation
Technology companies, banks, consulting firms, healthcare, retail, education, manufacturing, and startups
Excel, SQL, Python, Power BI or Tableau
Analytical thinking, accuracy, curiosity, problem-solving, and communication
Junior Data Analyst, Reporting Analyst, Business Data Analyst, MIS Analyst, and Product Analyst trainee

sections.heading: What does a Data Analyst do?

blocks.text: Data collection and cleaning
Collect data from databases, spreadsheets, APIs, and business systems. Correct missing values, duplicates, inconsistent formats, and data-quality issues.
Data querying and analysis
Use SQL and statistical methods to investigate trends, compare performance, identify patterns, and answer business questions.
Dashboard and report development
Build dashboards, KPI reports, charts, and interactive visualisations that make complex information easier to understand.
Business recommendations
Explain what the data shows, investigate possible causes, and recommend next steps to business or product teams.
Business Intelligence (BI) Analyst
Builds recurring reports, KPI dashboards, and performance tracking systems for business teams.
Product Analyst
Analyses user behaviour, conversion funnels, engagement, retention, and product experiments.
Financial Data Analyst
Examines revenue, costs, budgets, profitability, and financial performance.
Marketing Analyst
Measures campaign performance, customer acquisition, audience behaviour, and marketing return on investment.
Advanced analytics pathway
With stronger mathematics, statistics, and programming, progress towards analytics engineering, data science, or machine learning roles.
Other domains include healthcare analytics, supply-chain analytics, risk analytics, HR analytics, education analytics, and operations analytics.

This plan assumes a three-year B.Sc. programme. If the institution offers a four-year honours or research pathway, use the additional year for advanced analytics, an internship, research, or a substantial capstone project.
Year 1
Foundations
Build programming and quantitative fundamentals

items.text: Learn Python fundamentals, variables, loops, functions, lists, dictionaries, and file handling.
Study descriptive statistics, probability, algebra, and introductory calculus.
Master Excel formulas, sorting, filtering, lookup functions, pivot tables, and charts.

blocks.label: Learn SQL basics
blocks.text: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, GROUP BY, and aggregate functions.

items.text: Understand data types, data quality, and the difference between correlation and causation.

blocks.label: Year-end deliverable
blocks.text: An Excel-based sales analysis and a Python project that cleans and summarises a small dataset.
Year 2
Analytics
Develop SQL, statistics, and dashboard skills

items.text: Learn joins, subqueries, common table expressions (CTEs), and window functions in SQL.
Practise pandas, NumPy, and matplotlib for data cleaning, analysis, and visualisation.
Study sampling, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, and introductory regression.
Build interactive dashboards in Power BI or Tableau.
Learn data modelling, relationships, KPI design, and basic business analysis.
Explore introductory machine learning concepts without losing focus on core analyst skills.

blocks.label: Year-end deliverable
blocks.text: A SQL analysis project and an interactive dashboard with documented business insights.
Year 3
Employability
Build a job-ready portfolio

items.text: Complete two or three end-to-end analytics projects using realistic datasets.
Practise advanced SQL interview problems and analytical case studies.
Learn A/B testing fundamentals, metric interpretation, and experiment limitations.
Use Git and GitHub to document projects, code, and analysis.
Complete an internship, research project, or industry-oriented capstone where possible.
Prepare a concise resume, project portfolio, and interview presentations.

blocks.label: Year-end deliverable
blocks.text: A portfolio with SQL, Python, dashboard, and business-recommendation projects.

blocks.label: Optional Year 4
blocks.text: Advanced analytics

items.text: Work with larger datasets and more complex data pipelines.
Study predictive modelling, experimentation, and advanced statistical methods.
Explore cloud data platforms and data warehouses.
Complete a research dissertation or industry internship.
Specialise in product analytics, finance, marketing, healthcare, or operations analytics.

sections.heading: Technical and professional skills to master

rows.text: Excel formulas, pivot tables, lookups, data validation, charts
Joins, aggregations, CTEs, subqueries, window functions
pandas, NumPy, matplotlib, data cleaning and automation
Descriptive statistics, probability, sampling, hypothesis testing, regression
Power BI or Tableau, chart selection, dashboard design, KPI reporting
Data quality, relational databases, data modelling, documentation
Requirements gathering, metric definitions, root-cause analysis
Insight summaries, stakeholder presentations, clear recommendations
Git, reproducibility, privacy, responsible data handling

blocks.label: Recommended priority
blocks.text: Excel + SQL + Power BI + Python + statistics. These form a practical core skill stack for many entry-level Data Analyst roles. Machine learning is useful as an extension, but it should not replace proficiency in querying, cleaning, interpreting, and communicating data.

sections.heading: Software and tools to become familiar with

blocks.text: Microsoft Excel
Use for quick analysis, pivot tables, formulas, data validation, and reporting.
Microsoft Excel
SQL and PostgreSQL
Learn how to retrieve, join, aggregate, and analyse data stored in relational databases.
PostgreSQL
Microsoft Power BI
Build interactive reports, KPI dashboards, data models, and measures using DAX.
Power BI learning
Python
Use pandas and NumPy to manipulate data and matplotlib to communicate analytical findings.
pandas documentation
GitHub
Publish project documentation, SQL scripts, notebooks, dashboards' supporting files, and reproducible analysis.
GitHub

Other useful tools include Tableau, Jupyter Notebook, Google Sheets, SQLite, and a cloud data warehouse such as BigQuery or Snowflake. Choose one primary dashboard tool first instead of trying to learn every platform at once.

sections.heading: Portfolio projects to complete before graduation

blocks.text: Projects should show not just charts, but also the question asked, the cleaning process, analytical method, findings, and practical recommendations.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Retail Sales Analysis

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Beginner · Year 1
Analyse sales, revenue, average order value, product performance, and monthly trends using a public or synthetic dataset.

blocks.label: Tools
blocks.text: Excel, pivot tables, charts.

blocks.label: Demonstrates
blocks.text: Spreadsheet proficiency, KPI calculation, and basic business reasoning.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: E-commerce SQL Analysis

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Intermediate · Year 2
Use customers, orders, products, and payments tables to investigate repeat purchases, customer segments, sales trends, and top-performing products.

blocks.label: Tools
blocks.text: PostgreSQL or SQLite.

blocks.label: Demonstrates
blocks.text: Joins, aggregations, CTEs, window functions, and structured problem-solving.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Business Performance Dashboard

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Intermediate · Year 2–3
Build an interactive dashboard showing revenue, profit, conversion, regional performance, and time-based trends. Include filters and clearly defined metrics.

blocks.label: Tools
blocks.text: Power BI or Tableau.

blocks.label: Demonstrates
blocks.text: Data modelling, visualisation, KPI design, and stakeholder reporting.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Customer Retention and Cohort Analysis

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Advanced · Year 3
Examine repeat-purchase behaviour or user retention by cohort. Identify segments with different retention patterns and propose testable ways to improve engagement.

blocks.label: Tools
blocks.text: SQL, Python, pandas, and a dashboard tool.

blocks.label: Demonstrates
blocks.text: Analytical depth, cohort analysis, statistical reasoning, and business recommendations.

For every project, include a README with the business question, dataset source, data-cleaning steps, metric definitions, findings, limitations, and recommended actions. Never publish personal or confidential data.

blocks.text: Application strategy

items.text: Create a one-page resume focused on SQL, Excel, Power BI, Python, and statistics.
Publish three strong projects on GitHub and include screenshots or links to dashboard demonstrations.
Practise SQL daily, particularly joins, aggregations, CTEs, and window functions.
Prepare to explain one project from raw data through cleaning, analysis, insights, and recommendations.
Apply to internships as well as graduate positions, and track applications in a spreadsheet.
Tailor your resume to the advertised role instead of sending the same version to every employer.

blocks.text: Certifications can structure your learning and help demonstrate tool proficiency, but they do not replace practical projects or guarantee employment.

Optional credentials to investigate include the Microsoft Certified: Power BI Data Analyst Associate certification and the Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate. Check current exam formats, course requirements, pricing, and availability before enrolling.

blocks.label: Recommended order
blocks.text: Learn SQL and Excel first, add one dashboard tool, strengthen Python and statistics, and then consider a certification that matches your target jobs.

An M.Sc. is not mandatory for every Data Analyst job. Practical skills and experience can be sufficient for many entry-level positions. Higher education can be useful for advanced analytics, research, or specialised career paths.

rows.text: Advanced statistics, analytics, and machine learning
Strong foundation in statistical inference and modelling
Quantitative modelling and advanced analytical methods
Business strategy, analytics leadership, and management
Focused applied training, depending on the institution

blocks.text: Before applying, check admission requirements, mathematics prerequisites, curriculum quality, placement outcomes, and the amount of hands-on project work.

blocks.label: Recommended pathway
blocks.text: B.Sc. Data Science & Artificial Intelligence → strong SQL, Excel, statistics, and Power BI skills → Python analytics projects → internship → Junior Data Analyst or Reporting Analyst role.

The best strategy is to focus on practical analytical ability rather than trying to master every AI tool or programming framework at once. Employers need analysts who can work with imperfect data, select appropriate methods, explain what the results mean, and recommend sensible actions.
By graduation, aim to have a portfolio that proves you can take a business question from raw data to a clear, defensible recommendation.
